subject.title: MissingAgentHarnessError race: non-atomic harness registry clear+restore during plugin cache cycle

question: Which harness ownership classes should survive an empty plugin-scope reload: only approved always-on/native provider harnesses, every previously registered harness, or none with retry/readiness/doctor recovery instead?
rationale: Current main still clears the registry, but the obvious restore-all repair can change plugin disablement and empty-scope security semantics; automation cannot choose that product and ownership contract safely.

options.title: Preserve approved always-on harnesses
options.body: Filter restoration to the maintainer-approved always-on/native provider contract and prove plugin-owned harnesses from disabled or unscoped plugins are cleared.

options.title: Accept restore-all semantics
options.body: Document and test that previously registered harnesses remain callable across empty active registries, accepting the compatibility and security-boundary tradeoff.

options.title: Clear all and recover elsewhere
options.body: Keep empty-scope clears strict and solve user-visible failures with readiness, retry, or doctor/config repair paths instead of preserving harness registry entries.

recommendation.title: Preserve approved always-on harnesses
recommendation.body: Filter restoration to the maintainer-approved always-on/native provider contract and prove plugin-owned harnesses from disabled or unscoped plugins are cleared.

likelyOwner.reason: The harness registry and current lifecycle integration trace back to steipete's feature-introduction commit, making this the best available ownership route for the final contract decision.
